# TCS HR head clarifies headcount drop of 23,460 in FY26, says it remains on track to hire 40,000 freshers

**URL:** https://www.storyboard18.com/brand-marketing/tcs-hr-head-clarifies-headcount-drop-of-23460-in-fy26-says-it-remains-on-track-to-hire-40000-freshers-95229.htm
**Description:** Even as headcount fell sharply, TCS signalled confidence ahead. CEO K Krithivasan said growth momentum returned after Q1, while CHRO Sudeep Kunnumal maintained fresher hiring will continue at scale despite restructuring.
**Scraped:** 2026-11-17T15:04:01.957887+00:00

---

Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) reported a decline in its workforce in FY2026, even as the company signalled continued hiring momentum and improving business outlook.

The IT major ended the March quarter with 584,519 employees, a drop of 23,460 compared to a year earlier. Chief Human Resources Officer Sudeep Kunnumal said the reduction cannot be fully attributed to last year’s restructuring exercise.

He told The Times of India that the company has already rolled out [25,000 campus offers](https://www.storyboard18.com/brand-marketing/tcs-cuts-fresher-offers-to-25000-in-fy27-hiring-boost-depends-on-demand-report-ws-l-94895.htm) and remains on track to hire around 40,000 freshers annually. “Last year, we onboarded 44,000 trainees… we will continue to be among the largest recruiters across universities and the market,” he said.

Despite the annual decline, [TCS](https://www.storyboard18.com/how-it-works/tcs-trims-headcount-as-attrition-rises-and-costs-increase-ws-l-94668.htm) added 2,356 employees sequentially during the quarter through lateral hiring and fresher intake. The company has not announced a hiring target for FY27.

TCS said its layoffs cycle has concluded. The company had earlier announced plans to reduce around 2 percent of its workforce and tighten bench policies, leading to voluntary exits, particularly at mid-to-senior levels. “The restructuring exercise was completed,” the company said.

Responding to claims that the IT services sector could become irrelevant by 2030, Chief Executive Officer K Krithivasan said enterprises will continue to rely on firms like TCS to maximise the benefits of artificial intelligence.

Chief Operating Officer Aarthi Subramanian said there is a growing gap between rapid AI innovation and enterprise adoption. She told Economic Times that emerging AI systems are seen as a “big opportunity” for the company rather than a threat.

Krithivasan acknowledged the dip in performance but said it was linked to the end of a large transformation programme in the first quarter. He added that TCS recorded three consecutive quarters of growth after that and is entering the next fiscal with momentum, supported by a strong order book and international revenue.

The company said it will return to its standard salary increment cycle, which Krithivasan described as a sign of confidence in demand conditions. TCS also highlighted a strong deal pipeline, including three new mega deals and four clients crossing the $100 million annual revenue mark. The company aims to exceed its 4.6 percent constant currency growth recorded in FY26.

A separate controversy has also put TCS under scrutiny in recent days, with a major investigation underway at its [Nashik](https://www.storyboard18.com/brand-marketing/tcs-nashik-case-explained-sexual-harassment-conversion-allegations-timeline-and-probe-details-95187.htm) unit. Many women employees have accused senior colleagues of sexual harassment and coercion linked to religious conversion, prompting a police probe and multiple arrests.
